common: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied architectural visualization of the EXISTING apartment building. This exact image is the edit target, not inspiration for a new building. Produce one photorealistic landscape image at the SAME 4:3 framing, with identical camera position, perspective, daylight, shadows, sky, ground, trees, pedestrians, cars, bench, lamps, and surrounding buildings. Preserve EXACT building silhouette, stepped flat roof outline, height, number of floors, every window position and dimension, dark window frames, mullions, full-height glazed loggias, entrances, and all architectural geometry. Replace ONLY opaque exterior wall cladding. All existing white/pink HPL panels, gray opaque wall panels, beige brick and red lower brick become new brick; remove panel seams and original horizontal color zoning. Do not put brick over glass or alter metal mullions and frames. New brick is physically small ordinary approximately 250x65 mm face, horizontal running bond with half-brick offset and 10 mm recessed matte mortar, realistically fine scale for this ten-story building (about 40 courses per floor, not giant blocks). Matte softly textured ceramic brick with restrained natural brick-by-brick color variation. Sahara light sand-beige brick palette: #E3CDB2 40%, #F2E0CA 20%, #CDB79D 15%, #B09A84 10%, #987F6C 10%, #534036 5%, balanced creamy sandy appearance, low saturation 0.55, roughness 0.86, contrast 1.03, dark brown mortar #5A4A40. Flash dark brown-terracotta palette: #846651 35%, #6E513C 25%, #967B6C 15%, #4B3323 20%, #1A0C06 5%, muted rich brown appearance, saturation 0.75, roughness 0.82, contrast 1.08, mortar #3B322C. Hex codes are material albedo guidance: keep original daylight and shadow shading. Maintain original glass reflections. No text, labels, collage, watermark, additional buildings, changed landscaping, new decorative geometry or window frames. Output a single edited image.
variant1: VARIANT 1: Sahara dominates 75-80% of opaque walls from ground to parapet. Introduce only a few continuous substantial Flash vertical accents, about 20-25% of opaque wall area. Place the Flash accents on the existing solid vertical projecting separator pier around x=38% of image between the two glazed stacks of the left face, and the solid tall corner/return pier around x=68% separating the left sunlit face from right shaded face, with a corresponding rear-right separator if visible. Use existing architectural bay edges; brown runs uninterrupted full height on these selected opaque piers, wrapping their opaque returns. Keep the broad sunlit blank wall near x=62% LIGHT Sahara, and other wall bays light. Do not use a dark horizontal base band or dark top stripe. Do not outline every window or alternate many narrow brown stripes. Respect precise original openings inside any accent area.
variant2: VARIANT 2: A DARK BASE EXACTLY ONE FLOOR HIGH. Flash on every opaque wall of the first (ground) floor plus exposed plinth ONLY. Sahara on ALL opaque wall areas from the second floor upward right through the parapet, no dark upper bands, no vertical Flash accents. Important: the original red/brown base extends over TWO floor rows; it must be replaced such that its UPPER floor becomes light Sahara. The new boundary lies at the first horizontal floor division ABOVE the bottommost window row, halfway up the original red base, not at the old red/beige boundary. On the front sunlit face, this division slopes in perspective from roughly y=71.5% at the left building edge to y=67% at the main corner; follow the actual slab line above ground-floor openings. On right shaded facade follow the corresponding same first-floor ceiling line. Preserve all openings and glass completely, including tall glazed loggias through the material boundary. The light second-floor row must clearly read immediately above the dark ground-floor row.
